dial.summary: BTC Accumulation conditions intact on Jackson Hole Day 1 (Aug 27): BTC testing ~$80K with spot ETF inflows at a 10-month high ($1.92B weekly), BTC.D firm at ~59%, funding near zero—a textbook accumulation signature; macro backdrop broadly supportive with Global M2 expanding, ISM at a 4-year high (55.6%), curve steepening to +48bps, and DXY easing to 99.11 (neutral band); real yields at 2.35% remain the key headwind but are declining; Chair Warsh's inaugural Jackson Hole keynote tomorrow (Aug 28) is the decisive macro gate—a dovish-to-neutral tone alongside PCE softening toward 3% would be the green light for a sustained ATH assault, while a hawkish pivot would trigger rapid Risk Off repositioning.

indicators.name: Global Liquidity (Global M2)
indicators.note: Global 4-bank M2 aggregate (Fed/ECB/BOJ/PBOC) at ~$102.7T (latest available, ~6-week reporting lag); US M2 for July 2026 confirmed at $23,218B ($23.22T), 29th consecutive monthly increase, +6.11% YoY, record high; global M2 tracking ~$102.66T for June per MacroMicro (4-bank aggregate); no YoY contraction from any major central bank; 4-week uptrend confirmed; status supportive.

indicators.name: ISM Manufacturing PMI
indicators.note: July 2026 ISM Manufacturing PMI at 55.6% (released August 3) remains the most recent reading—August 2026 data releases September 1; sub-indexes: New Orders 56.7%, Production 58.5%, Employment 52.8%, Prices Paid 71.1%; highest reading since May 2022; 4-week trend up (June 53.3% → July 55.6%, +2.3pp); status supportive (above 50 and rising; headwind thresholds of <48 falling or >62 not met).

indicators.name: DXY (US Dollar Index)
indicators.note: ICE DXY at 99.11 on August 27, 2026 (+0.20% on the day as Jackson Hole opens); 4-week trend down: DXY weakened ~2.4% over the past month (from ~101.5 around July 27 to 99.11 on August 27), well above the 0.5% flat threshold; structural dollar weakness driven by US Treasury expanded long-term buyback program and rate cut expectations; status neutral (ICE DXY in the 97.5–100 neutral band; Warsh's Jackson Hole keynote August 28 is the key directional catalyst; a sustained close below 97.5 would flip to supportive).

indicators.name: Real Yields (US10Y - CPI)
indicators.note: FRED DFII10 at 2.35% as of mid-late August 2026 (down from 2.38% as of August 24); 4-week trend down: ~2.43% (July 25) → 2.35% (August 27) = -8bps, confirming the downtrend; status headwind (above the 2% absolute threshold despite the falling trend; a dovish Warsh keynote August 28 and soft PCE are the catalysts needed to compress real yields meaningfully below 2%).

indicators.name: 2s10s Yield Curve
indicators.note: August 27, 2026: 10Y yield at ~4.65% (down from 4.75% high on Aug 21), 2Y yield at ~4.17% (Aug 25); spread = +48bps; 4-week trend up: ~+35bps (July 24) → +48bps (August 27) = +13bps steepening, above the 5bps flat threshold; status supportive (positive spread AND sustained 4-week steepening trend intact; Warsh tone and NFP September 4 are the next key curve inputs).

indicators.name: Fed Balance Sheet
indicators.note: WALCL: $6,745,699M (~$6.75T) for week ending August 19, 2026 (H.4.1 released August 20); H.4.1 for week ending August 26 due out today August 27 (not yet released at time of update); 4-week trend flat: ~$6.70T (August 5) → $6.75T (August 19) = +$50B (+0.7%), near the 0.5% flat threshold; balance sheet holding at post-2022 stabilization plateau with no aggressive QT signal; status supportive.

indicators.name: BTC Funding Rates (perps avg)
indicators.note: BTC perpetual funding rate held near zero across major exchanges (Binance, Bybit, OKX) as of late August 2026; BTC tested above $80,000 on August 26 with spot ETF inflows at a 10-month high ($1.92B weekly); funding near zero despite price appreciation—a textbook accumulation signature (price up, funding flat); well below the +0.04%/8h overheating headwind threshold; 30-day trend down vs late-June/early-July elevated levels; status supportive. (CoinGlass unreachable via proxy—value held from prior run; rate consistent with observed price-funding divergence.)

indicators.name: Stablecoin Dominance
indicators.note: Stablecoin market cap ~$300-305B (late August 2026); total crypto market cap ~$2.74T (CoinGecko); stablecoin dominance ~10.9% (down from 11.06% on August 26); BTC.D ~59% (firm above 55%); 30-day trend down: ~13–14% (July 26) → ~10.9% (August 27)—capital rotating from stablecoins into risk assets as BTC tests $80K; status supportive (30-day falling trend confirmed; headwind condition—dominance rising while TOTAL rises—is opposite of current dynamics).

upcoming.title: Chicago PMI (August 2026)
upcoming.note: Chicago Business Barometer for August 2026 at 9:45 AM ET—released the last business day of August (Monday August 31); regional manufacturing cross-check against the July ISM surge (55.6%); a reading above 50 reinforces broad manufacturing expansion heading into the September 1 ISM release and pre-FOMC September 15–16 positioning.

upcoming.title: ISM Manufacturing PMI (August 2026)
upcoming.note: ISM releases the August 2026 Manufacturing PMI Report on Business at 10:00 AM ET—first post-Jackson Hole activity read; July 2026 ISM came in at 55.6% (highest since May 2022); a sustained expansion above 50 reinforces risk asset positioning; a collapse below 50 alongside a hawkish Warsh tone would trigger a Risk Off reassessment; pre-FOMC September 15–16 positioning begins in earnest.

upcoming.title: ADP National Employment Report (August 2026)
upcoming.note: ADP releases the August 2026 National Employment Report at 8:15 AM ET—private sector employment proxy arriving two days before the official NFP report (September 4); July ADP showed +44,000 private-sector jobs added; a weak reading would reinforce July NFP shock (−23K) and bolster the rate-cut case heading into FOMC September 15–16; a strong rebound toward +100K+ would complicate the dovish narrative.

upcoming.title: ISM Services PMI (August 2026)
upcoming.note: ISM releases the August 2026 Non-Manufacturing PMI at 10:00 AM ET—services sector counterpart to manufacturing ISM; services represent ~80% of US GDP; released one business day ahead of the August NFP report (September 4); a post-Jackson Hole services expansion reinforces the soft-landing narrative ahead of FOMC September 15–16.

upcoming.title: Initial Jobless Claims (week ended August 29, 2026)
upcoming.note: DOL weekly initial jobless claims at 8:30 AM ET for week ending August 29—first post-Jackson Hole labor read; sets early framing ahead of the August NFP report (September 4) and FOMC September 15–16; a spike above 220K reinforces the case for a cut; a stable-to-declining read keeps the policy debate open heading into NFP.

upcoming.title: Nonfarm Payrolls (August 2026)
upcoming.note: BLS Employment Situation for August 2026 at 8:30 AM ET—the last major labor data point before FOMC September 15–16; July 2026 NFP shocked at −23K (vs +79K forecast) and ADP July showed only +44K; a further contraction would strongly argue for a rate cut and would likely push DXY toward or below 97.5; a rebound toward +100K+ would complicate the dovish narrative; along with Warsh's Jackson Hole keynote (August 28) and CPI (September 11), NFP forms the trifecta shaping the September FOMC decision.
